title: Rehoboam
summary: Rehoboam is dated in Raleigh's chronological table (1617), column Iuda, by a yeere of the World. Jones, Appendix F (23rd ed., 2026), dates this and sets the sort.
description: Added from the Raleigh import (The History of the World, 1617). Raleigh is display-only. He gives a yeere of the World, not a BC year, and Jones, Appendix F (23rd ed., 2026), dates this and sets the sort.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (Floyd Nolen Jones): 1016 BC (no higher-tier year available).

birth.citation: Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics, 23rd ed. (Master Books, 2026), Appendix F, printed p. 279 (PDF p. 314)

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 787a
reign.note: Year cell "3713 3031 38". The third printed figure 38 is the column "Temple", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 17 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row. Column: Iuda..

reign.date: Sesostris, or Sesac, besieging Jerusalem in the fifth year of Rehoboam, A. M. 3033
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 186 (facsimile PDF p. 282)
reign.note: He equates Sesostris and Sesac with this siege. The event record is the sacking of the Temple in that same fifth year. The year is not Rehoboam’s accession.

reign.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxv
